Building ML systems for seismic event classification, catalog development, and geohazard monitoring in the Pacific Northwest.

Developed ML models to discriminate icequakes from tectonic earthquakes in Southern Alaska's seismic catalogue.

  • Built Random Forest classifier using 50+ waveform features; spectral features achieved 97.1% avg accuracy — best of all feature groups. Published in GJI.
  • Developed feature extraction pipeline with ObsPy and NumPy handling 10k+ multi-station events.

  • Designed low-latency real-time inference pipelines for in-vehicle deployment; integrated OpenStreetMap labels for GPS-independent road classification.

Publications

Peer-Reviewed Articles

Peer-reviewed articles and journal features · Google Scholar ↗

My research develops machine-learning methods for seismic event detection, classification, and characterization — benchmarking classical and deep-learning classifiers on large regional waveform datasets, clustering exotic seismicity (including "thunderquakes"), and building open tools for operational geohazard monitoring with the GAIA Hazard Lab.

1.
Akash Kharita, Marine Denolle, Alexander R. Hutko, J. Renate Hartog, Stephen D. Malone. "Exploration of Machine Learning Methods to Seismic Event Discrimination in the Pacific Northwest". Seismica, 5(1), 2026.
doi:10.26443/seismica.v5i1.2068  ·  arXiv ↗
Key findings: QuakeXNet (2D) — a 7-layer spectrogram CNN with 70,708 parameters — achieves 92% accuracy classifying PNW seismic events into earthquakes, explosions, surface events, and noise. Outperforms all classical ML baselines. Best out-of-domain generalization among tested architectures. Processes a full day of 100Hz 3-component data in ~9 seconds. Integrated into SeisBench; deployed via QuakeScope on AWS S3. Interpretability via Integrated Gradients attribution.
›
2.
Akash Kharita, Marine A. Denolle, Michael E. West. "Discrimination between Icequakes and Earthquakes in Southern Alaska: an Exploration of Waveform Features using Random Forest". Geophysical Journal International, 237(2), 1189–1207, 2024.
doi:10.1093/gji/ggae106
Key findings: Spectral features (97.1% avg accuracy) dramatically outperform statistical features (65.6%) for icequake–earthquake discrimination — robust to class imbalance and SNR variation. Kurtosis-based features are most informative among classical features. Model trained on high-SNR stations generalizes well across the seismic network. Also demonstrates a path for re-evaluating mislabelled events in historical catalogs.
›
3.
Akash Kharita, Amy Gilligan. "Cluster Analysis of Velocity Models around the Hudson Bay Region, Eastern Canada". Geophysical Journal International, 233(1), 359–375, 2023.
doi:10.1093/gji/ggac456  ·  ScienceDirect ↗
Key findings: Hierarchical agglomerative clustering (Ward linkage) of shear-wave velocity profiles at 59 sites surrounding Hudson Bay reveals 5 stable clusters correlating well with Precambrian tectonics and surface geology. Archean cratons (Rae, Hearne, Superior) are clearly distinguished from Proterozoic domains. New finding: Melville Peninsula profiles cluster with Ungava Peninsula, suggesting THO deformation extends ~650km northward.
›
4.
S. Mukhopadhyay, Akash Kharita. "Seismic Waves and Their Effect on Structures". Chapter 8 in Advances in Wave Dynamics (Eds. S. Chakraverty & P. Karunakaran), World Scientific, 2021.
Book chapter
About: Overview of seismic wave propagation and its effects on built structures — written during undergraduate studies at IIT Roorkee.
